hypotheses.title: Batch 87: Gold Quota Completion Sprint (Securing Alpha 28)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Combines three high-conviction, decorrelated quantitative strategies tuned for Gold Consultant qualification (Fitness >= 1.50, Sharpe >= 1.50, Turnover 10-25%, Uniqueness >= 0.85): (1) Candidate 1: The 8-PASS, 0.6356 self-correlated Free Cash Flow Yield engine tuned with platform Decay 6 to compress turnover to ~10% and propel Fitness >= 1.50. (2) Candidate 2: 1-Year LEAP Call Term Structure Contango vs 30-day volatility in TOP1000 Subindustry Neutral with Decay 6. (3) Candidate 3: 8-Day Linear Decay Microstructure Volume Absorption Reversion evaluated with platform Decay 8 to harness the 1.93 Sharpe engine.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if cash flow acceleration, options term premium, or volume shock reversion fail to achieve Sharpe >= 1.25 and Fitness >= 1.50 under platform neutralization.

candidates.expression: 0.60 * signed_power(group_rank(ts_rank(ts_backfill(actual_cashflow_per_share_value_quarterly, 60) / close, 180), subindustry) - 0.5, 2) + 0.30 * group_rank(ts_delta(ts_backfill(actual_cashflow_per_share_value_quarterly, 60), 90) / close, subindustry) - 0.10 * group_rank(ts_delta(close, 5) / close, subindustry)
candidates.rationale: Candidate 1 (Free Cash Flow Yield & 90-Day Revision Acceleration): Proven 8-PASS engine with low 0.6356 self-correlation. Simulated in TOP1000 Subindustry Neutral with Decay 6 to compress turnover into the ~10% sweet spot and lift Fitness past 1.50.

Candidate 2 (1-Year LEAP Call Term Structure Contango): Exploits the volatility term premium by longing 1-year institutional LEAP call IV relative to Parkinson realized volatility while shorting noisy 30-day mean IV. Simulated in TOP1000 Subindustry Neutral with Decay 6.

Candidate 3 (8-Day Microstructure Volume Absorption Reversion): Advances the 1.93 Sharpe volume-exhaustion engine by extending internal linear decay to 8 days. Evaluated in TOP1000 Subindustry Neutral with Decay 8 to compress turnover to ~20%.
